summary: Tested new Reset-Password-via-Security-Question feature (additive to existing Email OTP flow). Wrote 15 pytest cases (all passing) covering: GET security-question, register with/without security_answer, authenticated set/update security-answer, reset happy-path with normalized answer, wrong-answer generic 400, unknown-email generic 400, no-answer-set generic 400, 5-attempt rate limit -> 429 (even correct answer blocked while limited), short/empty password/answer validation, invalidation of pending email OTPs after successful security reset, has_security_answer surfaced in login response. Frontend E2E verified: /lupa-sandi shows both method tabs, security question text loaded from API, full security-reset flow succeeds with messy-cased/whitespace answer 'prabowo   SUBIANTO' -> redirect to /masuk -> login with new password works, sidebar 'security-settings-btn' label switches to 'Perbarui Jawaban Keamanan' after user has answer set, dialog save works, register form exposes optional security answer field. Regression: prior email-OTP pytest (9/9) still passes.
critical_code_review_comments: Anti-enumeration: same generic 'Email atau jawaban keamanan salah' returned for wrong email / wrong answer / user without answer set. Verified via pytest.
Answer normalization: lower+whitespace-collapsed applied BOTH at hash-time (register / set) and at compare-time. bcrypt hash stored (starts with $2). No plaintext.

Rate limit: 5 failed attempts in 1h correctly returns 429 on the 6th, and blocks even a correct answer while limited (verified). Note: rate-limit is on failed attempts only, so a valid user isn't blocked unless they've already accumulated failures — good.
Successful security reset invalidates pending password_resets records (used=true) — verified.
Sidebar button label updates via refreshUser() after saving security answer (has_security_answer becomes true).
Minor observation (not a bug): login rate-limiting is NOT applied to reset-password-security's *success* path — that's fine, per spec only failed attempts are counted.

Minor observation (not a bug): /api/auth/security-answer allows updates without any current-password/answer verification. This is acceptable because the endpoint requires a valid JWT (authenticated session), but if stronger protection is desired later, consider requiring the current password on update.
test_credentials: Ephemeral users created per test via /api/auth/register with prefix `test_sq_` / `test_ui_sq_`; DB rows cleaned up in fixture teardown.
seed_data_creation: None persistent. Test 11 injects a bcrypt-hashed OTP directly into password_resets to verify that a successful security reset invalidates it.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: `pytest /app/backend/tests/test_security_question.py -v -n 0`. Cross-file dependency-free. For UI: navigate to /lupa-sandi to see tab-based method picker; sidebar security-settings-btn is inside AppLayout (only visible when logged in). Use SECURITY_QUESTION constant text from server.py to assert question. When testing while logged in, note that navigating to /lupa-sandi from an authenticated session may redirect back to /dasbor (public route guard) — log out or use a fresh browser context to hit /lupa-sandi.
